etymologies.etymologyHTML: From daze +‎ -le, a frequentative form.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To confuse or overpower the sight of (someone or something, such as a sensor) by means of excessive brightness.

quote.citation: 1667, John Milton, “Book IX”, in Paradise Lost. […], London:  […]  [Samuel Simmons], and are to be sold by Peter Parker […]; [a]nd by Robert Boulter […]; [a]nd Matthias Walker, […], →OCLC; republished as Paradise Lost in Ten Books: […], London: Basil Montagu Pickering […], 1873, →OCLC:
quote.text: Those heavenly shapes / Will dazzle now the earthly, with their blaze / Insufferably bright.

quote.citation: 1834, Henry Taylor, Philip van Artevelde‎[1], volume 1, page 45:
quote.text: An unreflected light did never yet / Dazzle the vision feminine.

definitions.definition: (transitive, figuratively) To render incapable of thinking clearly; to overwhelm with showiness or brilliance.
(intransitive) To be overpowered by light; to be confused by excess of brightness.

quote.citation: 1626, Francis Bacon, Sylva Sylvarum: or, A Natural History in Ten Centuries‎[2]:
quote.text: For we see, that an over-light maketh the Eyes dazel, insomuch as perpetual looking against the Sun, would cause blindness.
[…] I dare not trust these Eyes; / They Dance in Mists, and dazle with surprize.

definitions.definition: (figurative) Showy brilliance that may stop a person from thinking clearly.

quote.citation: 1958, Laurens Van der Post, The lost world of the Kalahari: with the great and the little memory (1998 David Coulson edition):
quote.text: We were trying to stalk a dazzle of zebra which flashed in and out of a long strip of green and yellow fever trees, with an ostrich, its feathers flared like a ballet skirt around its dancing legs, on their flank, when suddenly  […]

quote.citation: 2009, Darren Paul Shearer, In You God Trusts, page 176:
quote.text: Zebras move in herds which are known as "dazzles." When a lion approaches a dazzle of zebras during its hunt,  […]

quote.citation: 2010, Douglas Rogers, The Last Resort: A Memoir of Mischief and Mayhem on a Family Farm in Africa, page 22:
quote.text: I reached the lodge as a dazzle of zebras trotted across the dirt road into thorny scrub by the game fence, and a lone kudu gazed up at me from the short grass near the swimming pool.
